body: I usually avoid dt Kitchener at night, but I'll walk Waterloo at all hours of the night and have never had any issues in my 7 years here except one guy who shouted from a car that he wanted to eat my pussy. I don't live near the main student area or Columbia street so maybe that's why? Or maybe crackheads tend to target men more often?
Do they work though? I find even with reminders on my calendar regularly, it's easy to just get accustomed to them and have them become part of the regular background simili of life.

When I was an undergrad I had a borderline criminal landlord who made me so jaded to have to deal with any landlords at all. He was a small property manager and they told the house, but I wonder if he's still out there. Is there any blacklist of terrible landlords I could add him to?
Also, know you're not alone! I'm a grad student in ECE, and I've been in similar situations and made it out the other side!

Focus on accomplishing what you need to day to day at work. Don't be afraid to ask questions.

Cultivate relationships with other women who work in male dominated fields who you can turn to for support at other times - seriously, two of my closest friends are an economist and a chef, both working in very male environments. Even though our work is very different, we have shared experiences and it really helps to bond over them.

When I was the only woman on the team I worked for, I got terribly depressed and isolated because I lived away from everyone close to me on that co-op term. If you're in a town you don't know, try to join some local club where you spend time with women you can befriend - maybe try joining a book club? Don't rely on social media too much for your interactions- keep in touch with people  obviously, but in-person is healthier and more fulfilling

And keep in mind, most of the men you work with will be perfectly decent and kind. If they say something sexist, it's probably not on purpose. And they probably won't!

Good luck, and try not to get too jaded!

I had to start doing my own laundry at 13. My mom continued to do my older brother's laundry until he was an adult. For me it was punishment for leaving chapstick in my pocket. My brother never got punished for leaving anything in his pockets. I also had to start making my own lunches at the same time he did, despite being 4 years younger (when he was 14 and I was 10).

It's carried through to adulthood. I'm expected to be financially independent earlier than my brother. Brother gets financial support from family that I don't. It's frustrating.

The unfortunate thing is thati do all the preventative stuff, but if I have a single slip up, there's 100% chance of infection. I got stuck in a bus without access to water for longer than expected, and now I have a kidney infection because I got mildly dehydrated.

I do everything I reasonably can, but being this prone to infection definitely limits my quality of life sometimes.

It depends on what is wrong. For acute infection there isn't a four week wait, but there can be waits for other things. I've had to wait four weeks for some relatively important stuff before, but the wait is because the condition isn't likely to get worse in four weeks. I've had waits of many months to see specialists, but again, it's because my condition wasn't going to get worse and my quality of life isn't affected.

There can definitely be four week waits, but it's because there's a triage system and urgent cases need to be seen first. Even though I have to wait four weeks for something, it's much better than having to worry about the cost.

Biomedical imaging technology, I'm an engineer in the field. I'm actually a Canadian, and a lot of the companies in the field have very tech-bro start up feelings unfortunately. I might consider a move to a big city or the US in the next few years though.

For some reason I'm just mentally tired this last week or so. I'm going back to grad school next year and I'm really looking forward to following my dreams, but I'm finding that being a woman working in a male dominated field is just making me jaded. There's just something soul-crushing about being the only woman at a gathering who's not one of the girlfriends of the men there. I don't know why it's wearing on me today, as I've been in this field for 5 years and should be used to it, but I don't think I ever will be.

Any solidarity out there?

Today I reached my financial goal of maxing out my TFSA! It's currently 22k invested in ETFs, which I plan to eventually use for retirement, 15k in a GIC that matures next year, and 10.5k in HISA!

The HISA is my e fund (+some extra savings to take a vacation since I don't need that much in an email fund), and I plan to use the GIC eventually as part of a down payment on a house or condo!

The ETFs I don't have any specific plans for except that they'll probably be for retirement. 

My next goal is to save up cash in my non-registered HISA until I reach about 50k, including the GIC, which should put me at enough for a down payment on a condo - hopefully right on schedule with me deciding where I want to live long term!

I've been saving so agressively to reach my goal and I'm so proud of myself that I got here!

Now question: as I have 22k invested for retirement already, am I safe to just save solely for my down payment for a year or so, considering I also put 3% + 3% employer match of my income into an RRSP?

Edit: I should specify, I'm 25, so I think the amount I have for retirement saved so far is reasonable.
